original_question: Given a modulus of continuity ω, construct a compact set K for which the Green function g_{C\K} satisfies two-sided pointwise bounds in terms of the distance to K. Specifically, if δ=dist(z,K), require constants C1,C2,δ0>0 independent of z such that C1·ω(δ) ≤ g_{C\K}(z) ≤ C2·ω(δ) whenever δ ≤ δ0.
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 2 (“Smoothness of Green functions and Markov Factors”), introduced there as the stronger pointwise version of Problem 1.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct target very closely: it is the pointwise two-sided estimate in terms of a prescribed modulus of continuity, uses the same distance parameter δ = dist(z,K), and correctly requires constants C1, C2, δ0 that are independent of z. This matches the paper’s Problem 2 rather than the weaker modulus-of-continuity formulation in Problem 1.
missing_details: The ambient setting should be stated explicitly: K is a compact subset of the complex plane ℂ.
The paper’s Section 2 works under the standing assumption that K is regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, so the Green function extends continuously to K.
The notation g_{ℂ\setminus K} should be defined explicitly as the Green function of ℂ \ K with pole at infinity.
To make the inequality logically correct, one should quantify over z in ℂ \ K with dist(z,K) ≤ δ0; if z were allowed to lie in K, the lower bound would fail because g vanishes on K.
Implicitly, K must be non-polar (equivalently, have positive logarithmic capacity) so that the Green function exists in the sense used earlier in the paper.
Problem 2 is an existence/finding problem for some K depending on the prescribed modulus ω; the paper does not, in the statement of Problem 2 itself, restrict to a special family such as K(γ).
refined_question: Given a modulus of continuity ω on [0,∞), find a non-polar compact set K ⊂ ℂ, regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, such that if g_{ℂ\setminus K} denotes the Green function of ℂ \ K with pole at infinity, then there exist constants C1, C2, δ0 > 0 for which, for every z ∈ ℂ \ K with δ := dist(z,K) ≤ δ0, one has C1·ω(δ) ≤ g_{ℂ\setminus K}(z) ≤ C2·ω(δ).
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of the paper’s official Problem 2 in Section 2. The nearby context matters in three ways: Section 2 imposes regularity of K with respect to the Dirichlet problem; Section 1.1 specifies that g_{ℂ\setminus K} is the Green function with pole at infinity; and Problem 2 is explicitly presented as a stronger, pointwise version of Problem 1, while Problem 3 is only the Hölder special case ω(δ)=δ^α (for K on the real line). The only substantive sharpening needed is to make the ambient complex-plane setting, the regularity/non-polar assumptions, and the quantifier over z ∈ ℂ \ K explicit. Also, the printed statement of Problem 2 appears to contain a typographical repetition ('C1, C1'); your use of C1 and C2 matches the intended meaning.

citations.label: definition of g_{ℂ\setminus K} as the Green function for ℂ \ K with pole at infinity
opening assumptions for Section 2 (K regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem; g_{ℂ\setminus K} continuous throughout ℂ)
